Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
19-year-old female with 3-day history of dysuria and mild lower abdominal cramps; features suggest uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI).

History:
• Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging pain on micturition for 3 days; mild crampy suprapubic pain.  
• Associated: Small episode of blood in urine earlier today; malodorous urine. No urinary frequency, urgency, flank pain, nausea, vomiting, fever, or bowel changes.  
• Gynecological/Sexual: Sexually active with new boyfriend ×2 months; uses condoms; never had STI screen; last menses 3 weeks ago; denies pregnancy likelihood. No vaginal discharge.  
• Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).  
• Medications: None regular. Tried OTC bicarbonate (dose/route/frequency not documented) without relief.  
• Allergies: Clindamycin – causes swelling (likely angioedema).  
• Social: College biology student; lives with friends; non-smoker; social alcohol use on weekends.  
• Family history: No known renal/urinary disease.

Examination:
• Vitals: not documented.  
• Physical exam: not performed/documented during tele-consult.

Impression:
Uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).

Plan:
• Empiric antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim, one tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact drug and dose not documented).  
• Hydration advice: Increase oral fluids; consider cranberry juice.  
• Sexual activity: Avoid intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.  
• Safety-netting: Return/call if fever, flank/back pain, worsening symptoms, or no improvement by end of week (possible pyelonephritis assessment).  
• Pregnancy: Perform home pregnancy test if any concern.  
• Follow-up: Re-contact clinic if symptoms persist or worsen after antibiotic course.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing elements: Vitals, physical examination, urinalysis, pregnancy test, STI screening, full medication reconciliation.  
● Conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise.
